_comment: The tutorial system's whole vocabulary, declared ONCE. Python validates
authored content against this file; the editor builds its dropdowns from
it; the JS engine evaluates exactly the predicate kinds listed here (a
test asserts the two agree). Adding a predicate or an anchor is an edit
to this file plus, for predicates only, a case in tutorial.js.
ANCHORS are why the CMS survives a redesign: authored content names an
anchor, never a selector. When markup moves, one line here changes and
every tutorial still lands on the right thing.

kinds.flow: A guided sequence — one or more steps, navigation under the tutorial's control. The FTUE shape.
kinds.announcement: A release note shown once per revision. Same machinery, different chrome; usually one step.

surfaces.modal: Centred over a scrim. No anchor. For openings, closings, and anything that is about the product rather than about one control.
surfaces.spotlight: The anchored form: the target is cut out of the scrim and a popover sits beside it. Requires an anchor.
surfaces.page: Docked in a corner with NO scrim and NO cutout — the whole page stays usable. For a step where there is more than one right control to press, so pointing at one of them would be wrong. Takes no anchor.

always.label: Always true
always.hint: A trigger that fires whenever the tutorial has not been seen.

first_run.label: First run — no production exists yet
first_run.hint: True while the install has never created a production.

version_changed.label: The studio updated since this was last seen
version_changed.hint: Announcement trigger. True when the running version differs from the version recorded the last time this tutorial was shown.

version_at_least.label: Running version is at or past…
version_at_least.hint: A VERSION string, e.g. 2026.08.05.83. Compared segment by segment.

state.label: Product state is true at…
state.hint: A dotted path into GET /api/state, e.g. stage_summary.screenplay. Truthy passes.

view.label: The user is on this view
view.hint: As a trigger and as an advance condition: true once that view is open.

api.label: The user completed a call
api.hint: { "method": "POST", "path": "^/api/screenplay" } — matched against successful calls only. This is how a step waits for the user to actually do the thing.

click.label: The user clicked this anchor
click.hint: Advances when the named anchor (or anything inside it) is clicked.

seen.label: Another tutorial was completed
seen.hint: Chains tutorials: this one waits until that one is done.

not_seen.label: Another tutorial has NOT been completed
not_seen.hint: Keeps two tutorials from competing for the same moment.

all.label: All of…
all.hint: A list of predicates; every one must pass.

any.label: Any of…
any.hint: A list of predicates; one passing is enough.

_view_note: Internal view names (what body[data-view] carries) do NOT match the URLs — the band was renamed after the router was written. The editor shows both so an author never guesses.
